text:
alex: Heads up — after the driver + pytorch minor bump rolled yesterday we're seeing ~2x p50 on tiny-batch workloads (N<=8). Putting a rollout hold on the driver on canary, but wanted to surface here.
maya: ack. any profiling yet? :eyes:
alex: did a quick nvprof / triton selection trace. Looks like the autotune now prefers a new matmul kernel variant for short sequences that increases per-call workspace/memcpy. snippet below:
```
TritonKernelSelector: chosen=matmul_mma_sp16x8_v3 workspace=832KB est_latency=0.65ms
previous=matmul_mma_sp8x8_v2 workspace=128KB est_latency=0.45ms
obs: memcpy/h2d increased +60us per call for N<=8
```
ryan: that's ... interesting. we also see increased kv-cache eviction churn in the same window (more memcpy + smaller batches => eviction frequency up). profiler flame shows frequent memcpy peaks between attention and kv insert.
devinfra-bot: ci/bench-smallbatch (canary) completed — regression +18% median, +95% tail 44% vs baseline. link: https://ci.internal/bench/31234
ci-bot: nightly-run 3123456800 — perf-farm flagged small-batch-p50 increased beyond guardrail.
maya: can you paste the triton autotune logs? maybe the autotune table got updated in the merge.
alex: pasted. also ran a perf counter dump:
```
pid 2345: memcpy_count=1024 memcpy_us_total=61000 avg_per_call=59us
matmul_calls=1200 chosen_variant=v3
kv_evictions=87
```
ryan: suspect change in selector heuristics that started favoring lower-compute but higher-memory-locality kernels when driver reports new scratch size. Could be driver report change or cublaslt fallback.
maya: plan: bisect between merges in the last 24h that touched triton selector / autotune table. I'll run a quick git bisect on infra/triton-selector.
alex: thank you. in parallel I'll add a quick heuristic patch to prefer previous matmul variant when sequence_len<=8 and workspace>256KB. should be low-risk for rollout.
ryan: +1 to heuristic patch as kill-switch. also add flag to pin kernel variant for specific models.
maya: bisect result: commit abc1234 introduced autotune table refresh and selector change (adds workspace-weight to score). reproduces locally.
alex: ok. reverting that commit or patching selector score would fix? maya: reverting abc1234 on canary fixes smallbatch numbers to baseline.
alex: opened PR to revert abc1234 and to add the temporary heuristic: PR 4321. tagging eng-runtime on it.
devinfra-bot: rollout hold set on driver-canary pool by alex.
slo-bot: alert — smallbatch p50 > SLO for last 10m, paging threshold reached. Ops team pinged.
ci-bot: created perf regression ticket #PRF-789 with attached bench results.
ryan: after revert we should run a targeted perf sweep across seq lengths 1..128 and kv workload to verify no regressions elsewhere.
maya: agreed. I'll run the sweep and post a summary.
alex: thanks all. once revert merges we'll run controlled rollout and monitor KV eviction metrics closely. :thumbsup:
maya: summary of next steps: (1) merge revert PR 4321, (2) deploy to canary, (3) run smallbatch sweep + kv-counters, (4) if green, gradual rollout. I'll coordinate.
ryan: tagging follow-up: add unit test that checks selector doesn't increase workspace by >x for smallseq path.
alex: sounds good. closing loop after canary sweep.
